related_questions.question: What are the bad side effects of the COVID jab?

text_blocks.snippet: While most COVID-19 vaccine side effects are mild and temporary, some individuals experience more severe reactions. Common side effects include pain or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, and fever. In rare cases, more serious side effects like allergic reactions, blood clots (especially with AstraZeneca and Johnson & Johnson), heart inflammation (myocarditis and pericarditis), and Guillain-Barré syndrome have been reported, according to the CDC.
snippet_highlighted_words: pain or swelling at the injection site, fatigue, headache, muscle pain, and fever

text_blocks.snippet: Common Side Effects (typically mild and short-lived):

list.snippet: Pain, redness, or swelling at the injection site .
Nausea or vomiting: (more common with Moderna).

text_blocks.snippet: Less Common but More Serious Side Effects:

list.title: Allergic reactions:
list.snippet: Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis) are rare but can occur.

list.title: Blood clots:
list.snippet: Some vaccines, like AstraZeneca and Johnson & Johnson, have been linked to rare cases of blood clots, particularly in women.

list.title: Heart inflammation (myocarditis and pericarditis):
list.snippet: While rare, these conditions have been reported, particularly in young men.

list.title: Guillain-Barré syndrome:
list.snippet: This neurological disorder has been associated with some COVID-19 vaccines, but the risk is very low, according to the CDC.

list.title: Severity varies:
list.snippet: Side effects can vary significantly from person to person.

list.title: Benefits outweigh risks:
list.snippet: The CDC emphasizes that the benefits of COVID-19 vaccination far outweigh the risks of potential side effects.

list.title: Seek medical attention:
list.snippet: If you experience any severe or concerning symptoms after vaccination, seek immediate medical attention.

list.title: Monitor for 15-30 minutes:
list.snippet: Individuals with a history of allergic reactions may be monitored for 30 minutes after vaccination.
